title: RBAC v2: add end-to-end integration tests for critical permissions (keys, roles, routing policies)
author: Leila Farouk
release_notes: Adds RBAC v2 e2e coverage for high-risk admin operations; prevents regressions where gateway/service authz checks drift or are bypassed.
description: Context: As part of RBAC v2 rollout we’ve been relying on unit tests + endpoint annotation coverage, but we’ve still had a few regressions where critical routes either (a) were reachable through alternate gateway paths (streaming vs non-streaming), or (b) had inconsistent enforcement between gateway and control-plane services. This PR adds end-to-end integration tests that exercise the full request path (gateway -> service) and validates allow/deny decisions for a small set of high-risk actions: API key rotation, role updates/bindings, and routing policy edits. What’s included: (1) New test harness utilities to create org/project/env fixtures and issue signed test tokens for users with specific RBAC v2 role bindings. (2) E2E tests for API key rotation endpoints: verifies that users without `keys.rotate` (or equivalent) receive 403 with structured denial code; verifies that a user with the permission can rotate and that the rotated secret is unusable/usable as expected. (3) E2E tests for role management: verifies deny-by-default on role creation/update/binding for a non-admin; verifies that Security Admin can update bindings; verifies that a user cannot grant permissions they don’t hold when `rbacv2_prevent_privilege_escalation` is enabled. (4) E2E tests for routing policy edits: verifies that Deployment Operator can update routing policy within the scoped environment, and that the same user is denied when attempting cross-environment edits; validates audit event fields include `authz.decision`, `authz.policy_version`, and `authz.denial_reason_code` when denied. (5) Runs the suite in CI as part of the existing integration pipeline (tagged `rbacv2_critical`). Notes: tests are feature-flag aware and run in dual-read mode; they assert behavior under `RBAC_V2_ENFORCE=true` and fail fast if the gateway is misconfigured (no authz middleware). Example assertion (pseudo): expect(deny).status==403 && deny.body.error.code=="PERMISSION_DENIED" && deny.body.error.denial_reason=="MISSING_PERMISSION" && deny.headers["x-redwood-denial-reason"] is present only for admin debug mode. Follow-ups: expand to audit export permissions once SUP-48219 fix lands; add Dedicated/Private matrix runs after we stabilize the base harness.
commits: test(rbacv2): add fixture builders for org/project/env + role bindings
test(gateway): add authz-aware request helpers + denial reason assertions
test(e2e): cover API key rotation allow/deny + rotation semantics
test(e2e): cover role update/binding allow/deny + privilege escalation guard
test(e2e): cover routing policy edits scoped to environment
ci: add rbacv2_critical tag to integration pipeline
review_conversation: Amara Diallo: Can we confirm we’re not only hitting the service directly? We need to ensure the gateway middleware is in the path for these tests.

Leila Farouk (author): Yep — all requests go through the gateway base URL in CI. Added an explicit preflight assertion that the gateway responds with the expected authz headers when debug mode is enabled; otherwise tests fail with a clear message.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: For key rotation, can we assert the old key is rejected across both the gateway and the downstream authn layer? I’m worried about caching.

Leila Farouk (author): Added a second call using the old key after rotation that must return 401; also added a short bounded retry loop (max 2s) to account for propagation since the authn cache TTL is 1s in the test environment.
Jordan Lee: Requesting changes: denial reason headers should not be present for non-admin callers. The test currently expects `x-redwood-denial-reason` unconditionally.

Leila Farouk (author): Good catch — updated assertions to only expect the header when `X-Redwood-Admin-Debug: true` is set and the subject has `authz.debug` permission. Otherwise we only check the response body denial_reason_code.
Benji Okafor: Role binding test looks good, but please add coverage for scope mismatch (org vs env) since that’s where we saw drift in dogfood.

Leila Farouk (author): Added `routing_policy_cross_env_denied` and `role_binding_wrong_scope_denied` cases; both validate the denial reason code is `SCOPE_MISMATCH` and that audit events include the attempted scope.
Marcus Lin: Approval after changes. These cover the exact scenarios we’ve been answering in SUP-48305 / SUP-48288. Please make sure the suite is stable (no flakes).
Leila Farouk (author): Ran the suite 20x on CI runners (see check re-run history); no flakes observed. Also reduced sleeps and switched to polling with a deadline for rotation propagation.
post_merge_notes: Added to the RBAC v2 rollout runbook checklist: verify rbacv2_critical suite green before enabling RBAC_V2_ENFORCE in a new environment. Next: extend harness to exercise Private installer bootstrap flows once the private env CI lane is available.
